source_text: Καὶ ἐκπέπληγμαι δὲ, ὁπότ᾽ ἂν ἀπίδω οἷα καὶ ὅσα εἰς βλάβην τῶν πέλας ἄνθρωποι ἐπιτετηδεύκασιν. Ἐπίσταμαι δὲ προαναρπαζομένους ἐνθένδε τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς καὶ γινομένους ἐκ ποδῶν, ἄνθ᾽ ὧν ἑαυτοὺς ματαιότητι δεδώκεσαν. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ οὐκ ἐφ᾽ ἁπάντων μετέρχεται ἡ τοῦ Θεοῦ πρόνοια ὀξέως διὰ τὴν πολλὴν ἀνεξικακίαν, οὐδὲ παραυτίκα τιμωρεῖται ἐπὶ ταῖς πλημμελείαις, τούτου χάριν οἴεται δεῖν ὁ πονηρὸς ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτάνειν ἐπὶ πλεῖον, ὡς ἀθῶος ἀπαλλάξων· οὐ συνιεὶς, ὅτι καὶ μετὰ πάμπολυν χρόνον ἀδικήσας οὐ λήσεται· ἀγαθόν γε μὴν μέγιστον, εὐλαβεῖσθαι Θεόν· οὗπερ ἀσεβὴς ἐκπεσὼν, οὐ πολὺν χρόνον τῇ ἑαυτοῦ μωρίᾳ καταχρήσεται. Χειρίστη δὲ καὶ ἐψευσμένη δόξα ἀνθρώπους ἐπινέμεται πολλάκις, περί τε δικαίων καὶ ἀδίκων. Ὑπολαμβάνουσι γὰρ περὶ ἑκατέρων τἀναντία· καὶ δίκαιός γε τὶς ὢν, οὐ τοιοῦτος ἔδοξε· καὶ πάλιν ἀσεβὴς, ἔμφρων ἐνομίσθη. Ταύτην ἔγωγε τὴν πλάνην χαλεπὴν ἐν τοῖς μάλιστα τίθεμαι.
thought_title: God's patience is no escape for the wicked
orientation: God's patience does not mean that the wicked will go unpunished.
pass_a_gloss: And I am astounded whenever I look at what sort and how many things men have practised for harm of neighbors. I know the ungodly being snatched away beforehand from here and getting out of the way, because they had given themselves to vanity. For since the providence of God does not pursue all swiftly because of much forbearance, nor punishes at once for offenses, for this reason the wicked man thinks he must sin more, as going to get off guiltless; not understanding that even after very much time, having done wrong, he will not escape notice; greatest good indeed to revere God, from which the ungodly having fallen will not use his own folly for much time. Worst and false opinion often spreads over men about both just and unjust. For they suppose the opposite about each: and someone being just did not seem such; and again an ungodly man was thought prudent. This error I place among the most grievous.

pass_b_english: I am astounded whenever I see what sort of things, and how many, people have devised to harm their neighbors (Ecclesiastes 8:9). And I know that the ungodly are snatched away from here before their time and removed from the scene, because they had given themselves over to vanity (Ecclesiastes 8:10). For since God's providence, in its great forbearance, does not swiftly pursue everyone, nor punish offenses on the spot, the wicked man supposes for this reason that he ought to sin all the more, as though he will get off unpunished (Ecclesiastes 8:11). He does not understand that even after a very long time the wrong he has done will not go unnoticed (Ecclesiastes 8:12). Yet the greatest good is to revere God; the ungodly man who has fallen away from this will not long have the use of his own folly (Ecclesiastes 8:12-13).

A very bad and false opinion often spreads among people about the just and the unjust. For they suppose the reverse about each: one man who was just was not thought to be so, and again an ungodly man was held to be wise (Ecclesiastes 8:14). For my part, I count this error among the most grievous.
notes: Numbering is the same in English and LXX. 'Removed from the scene' renders the idiom γινομένους ἐκ ποδῶν ('getting out of the way'). 'Fallen away from this' takes οὗπερ as referring to revering God; it could also refer to God himself ('fallen away from him'). 'Will not long have the use of his own folly' keeps καταχρήσεται ('make full use of'), Gregory's turn on LXX 8:13 'he will not prolong his days'. 'Held to be wise' renders ἔμφρων ('sensible').
